stories.headline: X‑RIC adds agents to telecom controllers
stories.body: **New benchmark pushes telecom AI:** X‑RIC layers reinforcement learning, behavioral cloning, and a transformer‑based Telecom Language Model onto O‑RAN's RAN Intelligent Controller for explainable, continuously refined control.
stories.why: Engineers can prototype AI‑driven network ops without building a full stack.

stories.headline: Steering agents police LLM multi‑agents
stories.body: **Low‑cost guardrails for LLM crews:** A steering agent watches LLM‑based multi‑agent runs, switching to cheap fast paths or expensive slow paths when goal drift appears, trained via reinforcement learning and group‑relative policy optimization.
stories.why: Keeps autonomous LLM pipelines from wandering off costly dead‑ends.

stories.headline: Linux drops AI tag, adds Meta review bot
stories.body: **Kernel code gets AI assistance:** The Linux project removed the mandatory AI tag and now runs Meta AI to suggest changes during code review, streamlining contributions without extra paperwork.
stories.why: Reduces friction for contributors while catching simple bugs early.

highlights.title: X-RIC: An Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning
highlights.summary: X-RIC is a new framework that adds agentic AI, including reinforcement learning, behavioral cloning, and a transformer-based Telecom Language Model, to O‑RAN's RAN Intelligent Controller for explainable, continuously refined control.
highlights.detail: The design integrates automated behavioral cloning using domain heuristics to improve sample efficiency, and embeds the reasoning module within the Near‑RT RIC loop for closed‑loop policy updates. It also introduces the BARX benchmark to evaluate agentic reasoning in the RAN domain.

highlights.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
highlights.summary: A steering agent is introduced to monitor LLM‑based multi‑agent executions and intervene with low‑cost fast or high‑cost slow paths when goal drift is detected, trained via reinforcement learning and group‑relative policy optimization.
highlights.detail: The system observes execution context to decide intervention timing and method, aiming to reduce wasted resources and undesired outcomes. Joint training of both paths combines a pairwise ranking objective with GRPO to improve alignment with overall goals.

related.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport

highlights.title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
highlights.summary: AI Consilium benchmark evaluates LLMs on 300 NEJM‑MedQA clinical cases, using physician‑calibrated judges to score 3,040 generated reports, finding structured reports improve management scores to 2.740 versus 2.436.
highlights.detail: The benchmark splits 110 cases for reference ratings and 190 for held‑out testing, and compares eight single‑model pipelines across free‑form and structured reasoning conditions. Model identity influences quality more than output format, and structured reports show advantages in several clinical dimensions.

highlights.title: How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering
highlights.summary: Meta released Forum, a new app for deeper Facebook group conversations, built using an AI agent integrated into the development workflow.
highlights.detail: Engineers adopted an AI‑native engineering approach, embedding an autonomous agent to assist coding, testing, and iteration, aiming to accelerate feature development and improve product quality. The blog post details the process and lessons learned from this methodology.

highlights.title: FAOPs: Normal Forms and an Algebra for AI Agent Workflows
highlights.summary: FAOP introduces a formal theory that treats AI agent workflows as typed functions with four progressive normal forms.
highlights.detail: The approach enforces traceability, auditability, and resource bounds by decomposing procedures into atomic steps, typing data flows, and factoring shared components. It aims to bring database‑level rigor to the design of multi‑step AI agents, facilitating safer deployment in regulated domains.

items.title: 2026 World Cup: Breaking Records, Spiky Charts and Reliability at Scale
items.summary: The 2026 World Cup set an all‑time infrastructure stress‑test record for Meta, highlighting peak load periods like New Year's Eve.
items.detail: The quadrennial event serves as a massive reliability benchmark, revealing spiky traffic patterns and prompting scaling innovations across Meta's services. The post discusses how these observations guide future system improvements.

items.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
items.summary: DeepMind announced the use of Google Antigravity to speed up discovery of novel antimicrobial peptides.
items.detail: The approach leverages advanced AI models to predict peptide efficacy, aiming to reduce experimental cycles and expand the searchable chemical space for antimicrobial candidates. The blog outlines early results and future research directions.

items.title: An update on independent evaluators
items.summary: Anthropic posted an update regarding its independent evaluators.
items.detail: The brief announcement does not include specifics about changes to evaluator processes, timelines, or any new metrics, but signals ongoing attention to third‑party assessment of model outputs.

items.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
items.summary: OpenAI launched the GPT‑Rosalind Academic Plan, granting eligible research labs sponsored access to the model and related tools.
items.detail: The program targets life‑sciences labs, offering free or heavily subsidized usage to accelerate research, though eligibility criteria and duration are not detailed in the announcement.

related.title: A model guide for the GPT-6 family

items.title: Sapienz Receives ISSTA 2026 Impact Paper Award
items.summary: Meta AI announced that Sapienz received the ISSTA 2026 Most Influential Paper Award for its 2016 multi‑objective Android testing work.
items.detail: The award recognizes a decade of impact since the research originated at University College London, highlighting Sapienz’s continued relevance in automated mobile app testing.

items.title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions
items.summary: OpenAI released a Brazilian Portuguese version of AI for Educators and Study Mode to support Teachers’ Day.
items.detail: The tools aim to help teachers guide students through step‑by‑step problem solving, but the announcement does not disclose pricing, rollout schedule, or integration details.

items.title: [$] Vendor hooks in the Android kernel
items.summary: At the 2026 Linux Plumbers Conference, Todd Kjos presented a session on Android vendor hooks and their role in kernel customization.
items.detail: Vendor hooks remain the preferred mechanism for out‑of‑tree changes in Android kernels, even as the platform moves toward a more generic kernel image.

items.title: Linux Kernel Drops AI Tag Requirement, Uses Meta AI For Code Reviews
items.summary: The Linux Kernel project removed the AI tag requirement and now uses Meta AI for code review assistance.
items.detail: The policy change follows earlier coverage of LLM‑generated contributions and reflects a shift toward automated review tooling, though specifics of the Meta AI integration are not disclosed.

items.title: Another Wireless Chip has a Hidden SDR Revealed
items.summary: A hidden baseband mode in the ESP32 wireless chip enables software-defined radio functionality.
items.detail: The discovery adds SDR capabilities to an already popular microcontroller, allowing developers to experiment with radio protocols without additional hardware. This expands the ESP32's utility in embedded RF projects, though performance may be limited compared to dedicated SDRs.

related.title: Various Projects Find Hidden SDR Capabilities in ESP32 Microcontrollers

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, and Red Hat released security updates covering dozens of packages.
items.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities across system libraries, language runtimes, and applications such as LibreOffice and PostgreSQL. Administrators should apply the patches promptly to maintain compliance, especially for the critical kernel and network stack fixes.

items.title: KDE releases documentary
items.summary: KDE published a documentary celebrating its 30‑year history and the evolution of its desktop environment.
items.detail: The film traces KDE from its 1996 inception to recent milestones, highlighting the Qt licensing dispute, the KHTML engine's influence on WebKit, and the controversial KDE 4 transition. It serves as both a historical record and a promotional piece for the community.

items.title: Seven stable kernels for Thursday with fix for critical vulnerability
items.summary: Seven stable Linux kernels, including 7.2.11 and 5.10.272, were released with a fix for critical CVE‑2026‑99999.
items.detail: The vulnerability affected skb_checksum_help(), allowing malformed IPv4 packets to corrupt network headers. Upgrading to any of the listed kernel versions mitigates the issue. Users of older kernels should plan immediate updates to avoid potential exploitation.

items.title: FAOPs: Normal Forms and an Algebra for AI Agent Workflows
items.summary: FAOP introduces a formal theory that treats AI agent workflows as typed functions with four progressive normal forms.
items.detail: The approach enforces traceability, auditability, and resource bounds by decomposing procedures into atomic steps, typing data flows, and factoring shared components. It aims to bring database‑level rigor to the design of multi‑step AI agents, facilitating safer deployment in regulated domains.

items.title: TraHist: Fast and Accurate Cardinality Estimation for Trajectory Data (Extended Version)
items.summary: TraHist proposes a density‑adaptive histogram estimator to improve cardinality estimation for trajectory data.
items.detail: By aligning bucket boundaries with spatiotemporal density patterns, TraHist reduces overestimation caused by traditional axis‑aligned histograms that split moving objects across partitions. The method retains the simplicity of histograms while better handling the dependencies inherent in trajectory datasets.

items.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation in S3-Compatible Object Storage under Client Concurrency
items.summary: The study measures per‑object ML‑KEM key encapsulation overhead against classical key exchange on an S3‑compatible object store using up to 500 concurrent workers.
items.detail: Two client implementations and two processor types were evaluated with pre‑registered experiments and statistical equivalence testing. The results clarify when ML‑KEM introduces latency and how it scales with client concurrency, informing cloud storage encryption choices.

items.title: Are We Testing the Wrong Quantum Bugs? A Study of Fault Representation Gaps in Quantum Software Testing
items.summary: An audit of quantum testing tools found they cover only a fraction of real‑world bug families, with 20 families supported by mutation tools and 15 additional families from curated benchmarks.
items.detail: The authors collected 410 bugs from ten quantum software repositories over two years and classified them into 56 families. Comparison shows a gap between represented faults and those occurring in practice, suggesting the need for broader testing suites.

related.title: QEDIA: Quantum Program Verification in Lean

items.title: Helix: A Unified Programmable Accelerator for Diverse Krylov Subspace Solvers
items.summary: Helix is a programmable accelerator that supports multiple Krylov subspace solvers with zero solver‑switching latency and reusable HBM buffers.
items.detail: The architecture abstracts common primitives across solvers, provides programmable datapaths, and includes a DSL compiler to map different algorithms efficiently. This decouples hardware from specific solvers, enabling rapid reconfiguration without hardware redesign.

items.title: ReFlow: Replay-Driven Decoupling for Efficient RL Post-Training
items.summary: ReFlow introduces a replay‑driven decoupling approach to improve efficiency of reinforcement‑learning post‑training for large language models.
items.detail: By separating rollout generation from policy optimization and using replay buffers, ReFlow reduces policy staleness while avoiding the quality degradation seen in highly asynchronous systems. The design adapts resource allocation dynamically to multi‑turn agent workloads.

items.title: ai-dynamo/dynamo
items.summary: ai‑dynamo/dynamo is a Rust‑based framework for distributed inference serving at datacenter scale.
items.detail: The project provides tools for scaling inference workloads across many machines, handling model loading, request routing, and load balancing, aiming to simplify deployment of large AI models in production environments.

items.title: google/googletest
items.summary: google/googletest is the GoogleTest framework for unit testing and mocking in C++.
items.detail: The repository offers a comprehensive set of assertions, test fixtures, and mocking utilities, widely used for verifying correctness of C++ codebases and integrating with continuous‑integration pipelines.

items.title: ChiR24/Unreal_mcp
items.summary: ChiR24/Unreal_mcp provides a Model Context Protocol server that lets AI assistants control Unreal Engine via the native C++ Automation Bridge plugin, built with TypeScript and C++.
items.detail: The server translates high‑level AI commands into Unreal automation actions, enabling real‑time scripting of gameplay or editor tasks. It works with the Automation Bridge plugin, so developers must have that plugin enabled in their projects. The TypeScript layer offers a convenient API for rapid prototyping, while the C++ core ensures low‑latency interaction with the engine.

items.title: Crosstalk-Solutions/unifi-toolkit
items.summary: Crosstalk‑Solutions/unifi-toolkit is a Python suite of tools for managing UniFi network devices.
items.detail: The toolkit includes scripts for provisioning access points, retrieving client statistics, and automating configuration backups. It targets network administrators who need programmable control over UniFi controllers without using the web UI. The tools are open source and can be integrated into custom monitoring pipelines.

items.title: Flare-Animate/Flare
items.summary: Flare is an open‑source animation suite forked from OpenToonz, written in C++.
items.detail: Flare retains the familiar OpenToonz interface while adding modern build tooling and bug fixes. It supports raster and vector drawing, keyframe animation, and plug‑in extensions. The project aims to provide a lightweight, community‑maintained alternative for animation studios and hobbyists.

items.title: LargeModGames/spotatui
items.summary: spotatui is a fast, standalone terminal music player in Rust that streams Spotify and supports local, Subsonic, radio, Qobuz, and YouTube sources.
items.detail: The player offers a responsive TUI with keyboard shortcuts for playback control and playlist management. It authenticates with Spotify via the official API and can fall back to other services, making it a versatile choice for users who prefer a console‑based music experience. The Rust implementation emphasizes safety and performance.
